lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Devices in total accounted for approximately 51%, 52%, and 52% of our net revenues in fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
Masks, diagnostic products and accessories together accounted for approximately 37%, 36%, and 35% of our net revenues in fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

During fiscal year 2026, we invested $378 million on research and development activities, which represents 6.7% of net revenues with a continued focus on the development and commercialization of new, innovative products and solutions that improve patient outcomes, create efficiencies for our customers and help physicians and providers better manage chronic disease and lower healthcare costs.
No single customer accounted for 10% or more of our total revenues for any of the periods presented.
various suppliers, including some who are single-source suppliers for us.

While we do not generally receive direct payments for our products from payors in other countries, our success largely depends on the ability of patients to obtain coverage and our customers to obtain adequate reimbursement from those payors.
Our distributors either repair our products with parts supplied by us or arrange shipment of products to our facilities for repair or replacement.
We rely on a combination of patents, designs, trademarks, trade secrets, copyrights, and non-disclosure agreements to protect our proprietary technology and rights.

• Our business depends on our ability to effectively educate and engage dealers of home healthcare products, sleep clinics and physicians, health care providers, and patients regarding the benefits of our products, software solutions and services.

The extent to which public health crises impact our business, results of operations, and financial condition will depend on future developments which are highly uncertain and are difficult to predict.
We rely on a combination of owned and licensed patents, trade secrets and non-disclosure agreements to protect our intellectual property.
Our ability to make payments on, and to refinance, our indebtedness, and to fund the future expansion of our business will depend on our ability to generate cash in the future.
We purchase configured components for our devices from various suppliers, including some who are single-source suppliers for us.
We rely on information technology systems and infrastructure, including technologies and services provided by third parties, to support our business processes and activities, products and customers.
Our business therefore depends on effective, reliable and secure operation of our technology systems and related infrastructure.

Our ability to manage our growth effectively depends on our ability to implement and improve our financial and management information systems on a timely basis and to effect other changes in our business including the ability to monitor and improve manufacturing systems, and implement information technology, and quality and regulatory compliance systems, among others.
The success of our business depends on our ability to market effectively to these groups to ensure that our products are properly prescribed, marketed and sold by these third parties.
In addition, our software products and digital health solutions increasingly rely on interoperability with third-party technologies and platforms, and other connected health technologies.
We depend on services from various third parties as well as our own technical operations infrastructure to distribute our Residential Care Software products via the internet.
In the event our facilities are affected by natural or man-made disasters, we could be forced to rely on third-party manufacturers.
If changes are made to this program in the future, it could affect amounts being recovered by our customers and subsequent purchases from us.
In addition, our AI capabilities depend on access to appropriate data, technology infrastructure and specialized personnel.

In September 2019, the FDA also issued revised final guidance establishing a “Safety and Performance Based Pathway” for “manufacturers of certain well-understood device types” allowing manufacturers to rely on objective safety and performance criteria recognized by the FDA to demonstrate substantial equivalence, obviating the need for manufacturers to compare the safety and performance of their medical devices to specific predicate devices in the clearance process.

While we have historically paid dividends to holders of our common stock on a quarterly basis, the declaration and payment of future dividends will depend on many factors, including, but not limited to, our earnings, financial condition, business development needs and regulatory considerations, and are at the discretion of our board of directors pursuant to authority delegated to our audit committee.
We strongly encourage investors and shareholders to review our financial statements and publicly-filed reports in their entirety and not to rely on any single financial measure.
Our principal sources of liquidity are our existing cash and cash equivalents, cash generated from operations and access to our revolving credit facility.
